title: Shadow Mirroring Pipeline: safe duplication, configurable sampling & cost throttle
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: We need a robust shadow/mirroring pipeline to safely duplicate a subset of production requests to candidate models (or model variants) for offline evaluation, drift detection, and quality comparison without affecting user-facing latency or exposing PII to unapproved models. Current ad-hoc mirroring is expensive, lacks sampling determinism, and provides weak isolation and cost controls.

Goals:
- Deliver a pluggable mirroring middleware that duplicates requests to one or more destinations with configurable sampling strategies.
- Ensure mirrored traffic is fully isolated from production inference (no side effects, no KV cache pollution, no logs leaking sensitive data unless allowed).
- Provide deterministic sampling (by user/request key), plus a reservoir and time-based sampling modes.
- Implement cost throttle and budget tracking so experiments cannot exceed configured spend.
- Emit per-request trace metadata and a diff-friendly result payload to the evaluation pipeline.

Constraints & non-goals:
- Mirrored requests must be asynchronous and never block the origin response path. Synchronous mirroring for low-latency can be explored later but is out of scope for initial rollout.
- We will not build a full evaluation service; this should integrate with the existing eval ingestion pipeline.

Design overview:
- Ingress point: edge router / request router (service: request-gateway) will call the mirroring middleware when a route is configured for shadowing.
- Mirroring middleware responsibilities: sampling decision, request sanitization, tenant isolation tokens, budget check, enqueue to mirror queue (Kafka/Redis stream), metric tagging.
- Sampling strategies: deterministic hashing of stable key (user_id/session_id) for consistent bucketing; reservoir sampling for early experiments with limited budget; time-based sample windows for smoke tests.
- Isolation techniques: strip or redact high-risk fields (PII) using a configurable sanitization policy; mark mirrored requests with a non-PII tenant id; disable KV-cache and side-effect hooks; apply a different rate limiter and quota bucket.
- Cost controls: per-experiment budget in cents with a configurable throttle that drops mirrored messages once budget is exhausted; backpressure policy to avoid mirroring storms (e.g., 1% of orig rate, capped and burstable).
- Observability: produce structured metadata to the tracing system (trace_id + mirror_id), counters for mirrored vs dropped, per-destination latency and error rate, and an experiment-level spend meter.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Middleware deployed to staging and toggled off by default via feature flag.
- Deterministic sampling mode yields stable buckets for a given key across restarts.
- Mirrored requests are never on the critical path for origin responses (verified by p50/p95 comparison).
- Sanitization policy is configurable and can be enabled per-experiment.
- Budget depletion triggers graceful dropping and emits an alert and audit log.
- End-to-end observability: mirror count, drop count, per-destination latency, spend reported in Console.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Mirrored payloads can leak sensitive data. Mitigation: default sanitization to conservative mode + security review and KMS policy.
- Risk: Mirroring amplifies traffic and increases cost. Mitigation: strict default sample rate 0.1% and budget gating, quotas per org.
- Risk: Candidate model backend may affect shared infrastructure. Mitigation: route mirrored calls to isolated compute pools (dedicated or dedicated-like) and apply lower priority scheduling.

Non-functional notes:
- Performance budget: additional CPU on request-gateway must be <5% p95 overhead.
- Storage: mirror queue retention defaults to 24h for fast processing, configurable up to 7d for long-running offline evals.

Integration points & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Shadow+Mirroring+Design
- Architecture diagram: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/mirroring-arch-diagram

acceptance_criteria: Deployed middleware feature-flagged in staging and can be enabled per-route/experiment.
Deterministic sampling returns stable buckets for same stable key across multiple runs.
Sanitization policy can be toggled and applied without code change (policy config).
Budget throttle prevents mirror execution beyond configured spend and emits alert and audit log.
Mirror metrics (mirrored_count, dropped_count, spend_cents, dest_latency) visible in Console per-experiment.
No measurable impact on production p95 latency (>5% increase) when mirror sampling set to default 0.1%.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): Implement mirroring middleware at request-gateway with deterministic sampling, sanitization hook, enqueue to mirror queue, budget check. Feature-flagged. (Liam)
Phase 2: Build mirror consumer adapters that route to evaluation pipeline, add per-destination metrics and trace propagation. (Data Eng)
Phase 3: Console integration for experiment creation, spend cap UI, bucket preview. (Console UX)
Phase 4: Security hardening: KMS tagging, formal security review, compliance testing. (Security)
Phase 5: Staged rollout to a handful of internal orgs, monitor for 2 weeks, iterate on sanitization and budget defaults. (SRE + PM)
